name: Expected value
purpose: Finds the long-run average outcome when different outcomes have different probabilities.
realWorld: Used for expected investment return, expected derivative payoff, credit loss, insurance loss and decisions under uncertainty.
plainEnglish: Multiply each outcome by its probability, then add.
whyItWorks: Imagine the same uncertain situation happens 100 times.
A 30% outcome is expected about 30 times; a 70% outcome is expected about 70 times.
Total payoff over 100 repetitions is 30 × first payoff + 70 × second payoff.
Divide by 100 to get the ordinary arithmetic mean.
This simplifies to 0.30 × first payoff + 0.70 × second payoff. That is why probabilities are the weights.
Therefore E(X) is a probability-weighted mean, not a simple average unless all outcomes are equally likely.

name: Option strategy recognition
purpose: Identifies common option combinations from their positions and market views.
realWorld: Used to express directional, volatility and range-bound views with controlled payoffs.
keywords: buy call and put same strike
plainEnglish: Recognise the legs and infer the intended payoff.
whyItWorks: A covered call is long stock plus short call.
A protective put is long stock plus long put.
A long straddle buys a call and put with the same strike and expiry, seeking a large move.
A strangle uses different out-of-the-money strikes and needs a larger move.
Calendar spreads use different expirations.

steps: Investor owns stock and buys a put → protective put.
Investor buys same-strike call and put → long straddle.
Investor sells short-dated option and buys long-dated option → calendar spread.
workedExample.interpretation: First list every long and short leg; then map the combination to the strategy.

trap: A covered call limits upside; it is not downside insurance.

name: Option Greeks intuition
purpose: Maps each Greek to the risk factor it measures.
realWorld: Used for option risk reporting and hedging.
plainEnglish: Delta-price, gamma-delta curvature, theta-time, vega-volatility, rho-rate.
whyItWorks: Each Greek is a sensitivity holding other inputs approximately constant.
Delta estimates the first-order value change for a small move in S.
Gamma measures how delta itself changes as S changes.
Theta measures passage-of-time effect.
Vega and rho measure volatility and interest-rate exposure.
